title: Derivaciones matemáticas justificadas — D30 Señales, audio espacial y acústica

records.name: Wave equation
starting_principles: Small perturbations around equilibrium; homogeneous medium; sound speed c constant.

derivation.justification: Linearized momentum equation for small acoustic perturbations.
Linearized mass conservation.
Adiabatic equation of state for pressure-density perturbation.
Combine momentum, continuity and state relation to obtain scalar wave equation.

assumptions: Small perturbations around equilibrium; homogeneous medium; sound speed c constant.
records.result: The acoustic wave equation derives from linearized momentum, continuity and compressibility.
limits: Linear acoustics omits nonlinear high-amplitude effects and boundaries.
dimensional_verification: p tiene Pa; ρ0 kg/m³; u m/s; c m/s.
∇²p y (1/c²)∂²p/∂t² tienen Pa/m².

records.name: Inverse square attenuation
starting_principles: Point source isotropic; free field; no absorption/reflections.

derivation.equation: Power P crosses sphere area A(r)=4πr²
derivation.justification: For isotropic point source, energy spreads over spherical area.
Intensity is power per unit area.
Substitute sphere area to obtain inverse-square law.

assumptions: Point source isotropic; free field; no absorption/reflections.
records.result: Inverse-square attenuation derives from conservation of power over a sphere.
limits: Reflections, absorption and directivity alter the law.
dimensional_verification: P tiene W; r² m²; I tiene W/m².
4π es adimensional; la ley supone fuente puntual isotrópica.

records.name: Doppler effect
starting_principles: Uniform medium; source/receiver velocities along line of propagation; sign convention fixed.

derivation.justification: Define sound speed in stationary medium.
Compute observed period from relative wavefront spacing and receiver motion, with sign convention specified.
Invert period to frequency.
Require denominator positive for this convention.

assumptions: Uniform medium; source/receiver velocities along line of propagation; sign convention fixed.
records.result: Doppler shift derives from change in observed wavefront period due to relative motion.
limits: Formula changes sign according to source/receiver direction; velocities are subsonic in this model.
dimensional_verification: f y f' tienen Hz=T⁻¹; c,v_listener,v_source tienen L/T.
Los cocientes de velocidades son adimensionales; periodo T tiene s.

records.name: Room impulse response
starting_principles: Room approximated linear time-invariant over measurement; same position/orientation.

derivation.justification: Define room response to unit impulse.
For a linear time-invariant room, output is convolution.
Use Fourier transform property.
Estimate response from a known excitation and deconvolution.

assumptions: Room approximated linear time-invariant over measurement; same position/orientation.
Para convolución continua, h_room tiene unidad inversa de tiempo cuando la transferencia global es adimensional; en tiempo discreto los coeficientes se normalizan según convención.
records.result: Room response is convolution because a linear time-invariant acoustic space superposes delayed responses.
limits: Room changes over time or moving sources require time-varying convolution.
dimensional_verification: x,y tienen unidad de señal; h_room(t) tiene T⁻¹ para convolución continua con ganancia adimensional.
En frecuencia, H_room es adimensional si salida/entrada comparten unidad; y conserva unidad de x.

records.name: Schroeder reverb time
starting_principles: Diffuse late field; volume and equivalent absorption area in SI.

derivation.justification: Approximate late reverberant energy decay exponentially.
Define decay by 60 dB in energy level.
Solve exponential decay condition.
Relate decay time to room volume V and equivalent absorption area A in SI units.

assumptions: Diffuse late field; volume and equivalent absorption area in SI.
La constante 0.161 se expresa en s/m para V en m³ y A en m².
records.result: Schroeder/Sabine reverberation estimates derive from exponential energy decay and equivalent absorption.
limits: Sabine is approximate and assumes sufficiently diffuse field; Eyring may be better at high absorption.
dimensional_verification: V tiene m³; A absorción equivalente m²; V/A tiene m.
Constante Sabine 0.161 tiene s/m; RT60 queda en segundos.

records.name: Binaural HRTF
starting_principles: HRTF calibrated for listener/head; direction and sample rate known.

derivation.justification: Define direction-dependent left/right head-related impulse responses.
Filter source independently for each ear.
Derive interaural time and level differences from filtered outputs.
Select or interpolate filter based on source direction.

assumptions: HRTF calibrated for listener/head; direction and sample rate known.
ITD se mide en segundos; ILD se calcula con cociente de magnitudes adimensional antes del logaritmo.
records.result: HRTF spatialization derives from filtering each ear with direction-dependent transfer functions.
limits: HRTF varies by listener; generic HRTF may not localize accurately.
dimensional_verification: ITD=τ_L−τ_R tiene s; ILD es dB de razón adimensional.
HRTF es transferencia presión/salida sobre entrada; convolución conserva la unidad de la señal.

records.name: Ambisonics encoding
starting_principles: Finite SH order; basis normalization and channel ordering fixed.

derivation.justification: Choose spherical harmonic basis.
Project sound field onto basis.
Reconstruct directional field from finite coefficients.

derivation.equation: rotate coefficients with Wigner-D or rotate sampling frame
derivation.justification: Transform soundfield orientation.

assumptions: Finite SH order; basis normalization and channel ordering fixed.
records.result: Ambisonics encodes a soundfield as coefficients in a spherical harmonic basis.
limits: Low SH order cannot represent sharp directional features.
dimensional_verification: Y_lm y medida angular son adimensionales en SI; a_lm conserva unidad de S.
La suma SH reconstruye el mismo tipo/unidad de campo sonoro S.

records.name: Equal-power crossfade
starting_principles: u∈[0,1]; signals synchronized; power convention assumes uncorrelated/ideal channels.

derivation.justification: Choose quarter-circle gains for u∈[0,1].
Prove constant sum of squared gains.
Mix both signals through crossfade.
Check endpoint behavior.

assumptions: u∈[0,1]; signals synchronized; power convention assumes uncorrelated/ideal channels.
records.result: Equal-power crossfade derives from trigonometric gains whose squared sum is one.
limits: Equal power does not guarantee constant perceived loudness for correlated signals.
dimensional_verification: u, g_A y g_B son adimensionales; x_A,x_B,y comparten unidad de señal.
La potencia media constante requiere señales no correlacionadas o hipótesis estadísticas equivalentes.

records.name: Low-pass filter
starting_principles: f_s>0; cutoff below Nyquist; α in stable range.

derivation.justification: Define first-order recursive low-pass.
Take z-transform of recurrence.
Choose coefficient from exponential pole matching for cutoff f_c and sample rate f_s.
Ensure stable pole magnitude below one.

assumptions: f_s>0; cutoff below Nyquist; α in stable range.
records.result: A first-order low-pass derives from a one-pole recursive filter and exponential coefficient.
limits: One-pole filter is not brick-wall; coefficient approximation depends on discretization.
dimensional_verification: f_c y f_s tienen T⁻¹; f_c/f_s y α son adimensionales.
x[n], y[n] conservan unidad de señal.

records.name: Envelope follower
starting_principles: τ_attack,τ_release>0; input and envelope same amplitude scale.

derivation.justification: Convert time constant τ to discrete smoothing coefficient.
Apply exponential smoothing to magnitude.
Use faster/slower time constant for attack and release.
Map envelope to scale, emission or motion with a bounded transfer function.

assumptions: τ_attack,τ_release>0; input and envelope same amplitude scale.
records.result: Envelope follower derives from discrete exponential smoothing with separate attack/release constants.
limits: Envelope smoothing is an amplitude follower, not a full loudness/perceptual model.
dimensional_verification: τ_attack y τ_release tienen T; f_s T⁻¹; 1/(τ f_s) es adimensional.
a y env smoothing son adimensionales; env conserva unidad de |x|.

checks: Cada derivación incluye pasos justificados, supuestos, límites y verificación dimensional
Wave equation, inverse square y Doppler conservan unidades acústicas
RIR/HRTF distinguen convolución continua de discreta y tipan impulso
Sabine produce RT60 en segundos con constante SI
Ambisonics, crossfade, filtros y envelope follower mantienen escalas de señal coherentes
limitations: Los modelos son acústicos idealizados; respuesta real de sala, HRTF individual, absorción dependiente de frecuencia y percepción de loudness requieren calibración y pruebas.
